title: Ops Kiosk: microflow kiosk and contextual quick-fix executor
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Build a lightweight, searchable ops kiosk UI that exposes a curated set of small, idempotent microflows (pre-approved repair steps) for on-call and support engineers. The kiosk is intended to shorten mean-time-to-repair for common issues while preserving safety via RBAC, dry-run previews, and automatic audit logs.
proposal: Create a single-page kiosk embedded in the Console (ops > kiosk) that lists contextual microflows based on route/service/alert tags. Each microflow is a templated sequence of 1-3 guarded actions (e.g., flush cache, rotate token, restart worker shard) implemented as runbook-as-task primitives. The kiosk will show a concise intention, estimated impact, required permissions, and a dry-run output before any mutation. High-risk flows require a two-step approval (peer + automated safety checks). All executions produce structured audit artifacts (who, what, before/after, telemetry link) written to the private audit log and surfaced in the Console timeline.
tasks: Design API contract for microflow primitives (start/dryrun/commit/cancel) and stable JSON schema for inputs/outputs
Implement backend microflow registry service with RBAC and approval gating (authz checks against SSO groups)
Console: kiosk UI with search, context filters (service, route, alert id), and dry-run preview modal
Create 12 initial microflows for common support actions (cache-clear, key-rotate-safe, scaled-restart, payment-queue-unblock)
Instrumentation: emit structured telemetry and itemized token/cost estimates per run
Safety: integrate canary/rollback hooks and automatic rollback for non-idempotent failure modes
Docs: runbook templates, how to add new microflows, and postmortem checklist for manual escalation
acceptance_criteria: Kiosk UI lists microflows filtered by service tag and returns dry-run output identical to backend simulation
Execution path writes an audit record with before/after state link and correlates to trace id
RBAC prevents any user without 'support:execute' from committing mutations; dry-run still allowed for observers
High-risk flows require at least one peer approval recorded in the audit entry before commit
At least 8 of the 12 initial microflows are validated by Support during a dry-run rehearsal session
Latency: dry-run preview returns results within 3s for simple microflows and within 15s for multi-step simulations
notes: Progress: initial API spec drafted (doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Kiosk+API+Spec). Backend prototype spun up in feature branch ops/kiosk-proto.
